**Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member onboarding** – no standardised pathway from signup → first class → habit formation (critical for churn prevention)
- **Churn & win-back** – no documented trigger points, outreach cadence, or re-engagement playbook
- **Member check-ins** – no scheduled touchpoint system (30/60/90 day health checks, milestone celebration)
- **Pause/cancellation handling** – no pre-cancellation save process or pause protocol (retention lever you're leaving on the table)
- **Referral programme** – no mechanics, incentives, or member communication flow
- **Class quality audit** – no coaching standards enforcement or consistency check across instructors
- **Member data, privacy & GDPR** – no documented data handling, consent, or retention/deletion process (legal/compliance risk)
- **Coaching development roadmap** – no progression path, skill assessment, or upskilling cadence for coaches
- **New quarter programme launch** – no rollout SOP (comms, class scheduling, member messaging, coach briefing)
- **Supply ordering** – no vendor management, stock levels, or reorder triggers
- **Complaints & incidents** – no escalation path, documentation, or resolution SOP (duty of care issue)

**Needs updating**

- **Clients SOPs (23/33)** – likely missing specifics on: member goal-setting, outcome tracking, milestone communication, transformation documentation
- **Coaches SOPs (20/24)** – gaps in: weekly task management, performance feedback loops, sub/cover protocols, client handoff procedures
- **Marketing SOPs (5/5)** – probably light on: member lifecycle email sequences, retention marketing, referral comms, seasonal campaigns
- **Facilities (5/6)** – check if includes: emergency protocols, incident reporting, safeguarding/

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**1. Audit what you're ACTUALLY selling right now**
Before writing anything down, get your coaches together for 30 mins. Ask: "What do members ask for most?" and "What are we doing that we never explicitly mention?" You'll find revenue gaps (like personalized programming that isn't priced) and service confusion you didn't know existed.

**2. Price backwards from your unit economics, not feelings**
Don't guess. Calculate: monthly rent/utilities ÷ target members = minimum per-member revenue needed. Then layer on: coach hourly rate × hours per service × profit margin. This stops you underpricing group classes or overpricing PT. Get a template from Equinox or Barry's to see how they tier it (it'll shock you how simple it is).

**3. Create TWO separate documents, not one hybrid**
**Coach version:** What services exist, costs to run them, margin targets, and how to sell them (this is YOUR playbook). **Member version:** Clean pricing, what's included, no internal jargon. Member version gets laminated or lives as a downloadable PDF; coach version is a one-pager they reference during consultations.

**4. Test the menu with your top 3 members first**
Before rolling out, show pricing to members who already trust you. They'll spot if a class package is confusing or if PT pricing feels misaligned. One conversation might reveal you need a "starter PT package" that doesn't exist yet.

**Insights**

• **July was the inflection point** – you cracked something. Cost/lead crashed from £21 (June) to £2 (July), volume surged 10× to 215 leads, and you got your first 29 sales (13% close rate). August held the cost/lead steady at £3 but on a fraction of the spend (£144 vs £515), suggesting you've either paused top-performing campaigns or hit budget caps mid-month. The close rate jumped to 32% in August, which is strong, but you're starving the engine.

• **Your creative or targeting unlocked something in late July** – the dramatic shift in unit economics tells us it wasn't just "more spend." You've either found a winning audience segment, a creative angle that resonates, or both. The June-to-July jump is too sharp to be organic growth.

• **August reveals the real issue: underfunding, not underperformance.** At £3/lead with a 32% close rate, you're converting at roughly £9.37 per sale (before accounting for trial-to-membership conversion). That's working. You've cut spend to a quarter of July's level; you're leaving revenue on the table.

---

**Actions**

1. **Immediately revert to July's spend level (£500–600/month minimum) and identify what changed.** Pull the July campaign breakdown by ad set, creative, and audience. Which specific ad set or audience drove that 215-lead month? Duplicate it exactly. Don't guess – audit the campaign structure in Ads Manager. If you can't pinpoint it, you've got a data-tracking problem that needs fixing first (check your pixel and conversion API setup).

# REVENUE — GROW IT HARD

- **Rev/member has collapsed to £124 (July) — down from £138 (April) and £132 (Dec). Root cause: membership price too low or too many discounted/trial members in the cohort.** Action: audit current membership tiers immediately. If base rate is under £25/month, raise it 8–12% (to £27–28). Enforce no free trials; offer first month at 50% instead. This alone recovers £1,200–1,500/month at current headcount.

- **Churn spiked to 12.7% in May after the move; now stabilised at 3.3–7.6%.** The relocation worked. Now lock in: introduce a 12-month loyalty discount (£2–3/month off, tied to direct debit) to drop baseline churn to <3%. This protects the 159 members you've built.

- **Classes filling unevenly — peak hours full, off-peak (9 a.m., lunchtime, Sunday) under 60% capacity.** Introduce dynamic pricing: 10% discount on 9–11 a.m. and 13–14 p.m. slots to shift demand, or bundle 4× off-peak classes into a "Flex" membership tier at £18/month (vs standard £25+). Target: fill quiet slots by 20%, adds ~£800/month.

- **No visible add-on revenue.** Launch: personal training packages (3-session starter at £45, recurring memberships at £12/month per PT slot), nutrition/supplement retail (20% margin, stock 3–4 lines), and class passes for non-members (£4 per drop-in, upsell to membership). Conservatively: £400/month by month 3.

---

# EXPENSES — CUT THE SLACK

- **Cash outflows volatile: £16.5k–£39k (April excluded). Last 3 months avg £18.6k; prior 3 avg £19.9k.** Review variable cost split: utilities, supplies, contractor/PT wages. If any supplier is >8% of revenue, renegotiate or switch. Likely targets: lease (negotiate 5% reduction citing move success), cleaning/laundry (consolidate to 1 provider), equipment maintenance (move to ad-hoc vs monthly retainer if usage is low).
